newsitem.title: INDIA: India strike disrupts trains, police on alert.
newsitem.headline: India strike disrupts trains, police on alert.

text.p: A strike in a western Indian state disrupted railway services in the financial capital of Bombay on Monday, but government officials said the situation was relatively uneventful.
"There is tension in Nagpur, Kolhapur and parts of Maharashtra," Gopinath Munde, deputy chief minister of Maharashtra state, told Reuters. "But there is no untoward incident or police firing."

Opposition parties called a protest strike in Maharashtra after 12 people died when police opened fire to control a riot that erupted on Friday when the statue of a revered social activist was garlanded with shoes.
Activity in Bombay was paralysed over the weekend, following a protest strike call on Saturday. Monday's strike is also to protest the same incident, but Bombay has been excluded.

A Central Railway spokesman told Reuters that trains between Kurla and Thane stations on the suburban railway network had been halted for more than three hours by intermittent incidents of stone-throwing.
"In many places people have pulled sleepers onto the tracks, or are sitting on the rails," he said.

Thousands of the roughly three million commuters who rely on the trains to get to work each day found themselves stranded. They had to get off and walk along the tracks to the nearest railway station.
Groups of protestors had gathered at important points along the road and rail routes into the city, officials said. They shouted slogans or threw stones at vehicles defying the strike.
Munde said the situation was particularly tense on the National Highway at Shahapur in Thane district, about 28 kms (18 miles) northeast of Bombay, but the situation was under control.
"There was an attempt to burn a police chowki (post) in Nagpur, but the attempt was foiled," Munde said. The city of Nagpur is located roughly 600 km east of Bombay.
Munde said authorities had deployed 75 companies of the State Reserve Police (SRP) across the state.
"We have asked the centre for 20 companies of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), and we are still pursuing the request," Munde said.
More than 2,100 people have been arrested in Bombay to prevent them from stirring up more violence, Munde said.
In addition, 35 suspects were arrested in connection with the ransacking of the residence of Congress Opposition Leader Chhagan Bhujbal, Munde added.
